A flip of that argmin between CPU and MPS changes the output frame and fails the elementwise gate by O(1) regardless of tolerance; the user decided on 2026-10-28 to keep the cpu_parity rule as written, so a red cpu_parity is reported as is (exit 5, evidence retained)

r2.reason: it cannot complete in this build: pipeline.py ExplicitPrecisionDA3 disables autocast and casts the whole network to float16, while upstream CameraDec.forward hard-codes self.fc_t(feat.float()). The fp32 input meets an fp16 Linear and CPU raises 'mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype, but got Float and Half'; this was reproduced independently by V9.T46 (.venv, torch 2.3.1) and by the lead in envs/teachers/.venv-t6 (torch 2.14.1), CPU only, no DA3 weights. On MPS the lead reported a Metal assertion that aborts the process (SIGABRT, exit 134); no crash log was kept, so this is a report, not an independently reproduced fact, and the removal does not depend on it. It is the last stage of DA3-SMALL, so it would fail before DA3-BASE starts, and the authorization is already reserved and not refunded
r2.not_replaced: no substitute fp16 control is introduced; option B (autocast-based fp16 in pipeline.py) was not chosen, so pipeline.py is unchanged and its SHA bindings remain valid. If an fp16 consistency gate is wanted later: torch.autocast(device_type='mps') constructs in envs/teachers/.venv-t6 (torch 2.14.1), but model/da3.py:139 wraps the depth head and the camera estimation in autocast(enabled=False), so an outer autocast leaves those parts outside fp16. That would be a partial-fp16 gate and needs its own pre-registration stating what it covers
